Oslo Business School is expanding and invites applications for 1-2 faculty positions in accounting. The formal recruitment will be at the associate professor level with tenure. Candidates who qualify may be promoted to full professor following their appointment.

jobs.occupation: PhD position in marine biology in the EU project “Remedies”
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Biology (IBI) at NV faculty has a vacant 3-year PhD position for a marine macroalgae research in the Marine Sciences section  The position is part of a NTNU well known niche nationally using enabling technology for research and education of algal (phytoplankton, ice algae, macroalgae) dynamics to provide knowledge needed for better ecosystem function and management. This position will be shared with researchers at Department of Biotechnology and Food Science (IBT) focusing on biochemistry (also at NV faculty at NTNU). In addition, the PhD will also collaborate with SINTEF Industry (Department of Biotechnology and Nanomedicine) focusing on industrial applications. 

The overarching aim of the Marine Sciences section is focused on sustainable management, production, and utilization of biological marine resources. The announced position will be important in utilizing the momentum in educating the next NTNU generation of marine scientists using enabling technologies to understand, monitor and improve ecosystem health including reduction of human induced stress in the environment. Our departments do work with industry to find solutions and enhance the understanding of ecosystem function to utilize resources in a benign manner to provide “good ecology = good economy”.

The PhD candidate will be part of the EU Horizon project “Restoring ocean and waters in waterfront cities and their ports”. The specific objectives are to 1) protect and restore marine and freshwater ecosystems and biodiversity, 2) prevent and eliminate pollution of our ocean, seas and waters and 3) make a blue economy sustainable, carbon neutral and circular.

In Trondheim, our major environmental challenge is sewage and industry wastewater discharge into the Trondheimsfjord, inducing multiple stressors for marine production and biodiversity. Cascade effects, including replacements of kelp species with filamentous algae (“turf”), loss of fish and poor water quality.

Remedies approach: Restore declining population and habitats, including cultivation of kelp to remove excessive nutrients, heavy metals and provide biomass for products in the new blue economy. Our goal is to contribute to reduced pollution, better restoration, maintenance of biodiversity and improved water quality.

The main activities for the PhD will be to contribute to ensure habitat functions in macroalgae along coastal areas near Trondheim (restoration) which also include cultivation of seaweed at sites with different degrees of pollution level (e.g. nutrient loads and heavy metals). Identification, mapping and monitoring macroalgal growth zones and key environmental variables such as light, temperature, salinity, nutrient loads (e.g. nitrate, phosphate, silicate) by using different robotic platforms (using the operation pyramid comprising mini satellites, aerial drones, autonomous surface and underwater vehicles and moorings) in collaboration with Applied Underwater Robotic laboratory (NTNU) and Fjordlab (part of Ocean Space Centre in Trondheim of (NTNU & SINTEF) will be carried out.

The seaweed elemental composition will be analyzed for using cultivated seaweed as bioindicators (uptake of nutrients and pollutants), and biorefinery, including product development, for selected applications will be part of the project.

The hired candidate will be able to join a dynamic, cross-disciplinary team that is working on the development of new techniques to provide ecological, physiological and biochemical information needed for enhanced environmental monitoring and corresponding industrial applications.

The primary workplace will be at the Trondheim Biological Station, but changes in the place of work may occur during the project period.

Your immediate leader will be the head of the department of Biology.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Provide time-series of Key Environmental Variables (KEV) in Trondheimsfjord and corresponding growth dynamics of selected macroalgal species comprising brown, red and green macroalgae
• Model species for natural habitats and growth cultures will be the kelp species Saccharina latissima and Alaria esculenta and the brown wreck Fucus vesiculosus
• Combine information on elemental composition and ecophysiology (eg. photosynthetic parameters and pigment composition) in model species to use the algae as bioindicators of water quality and habitat stress level
• Chemical characterisation of seaweed biomass (cultivated, from restoration areas and from wild populations)
• Development of sequential biorefinery on cultivated biomass (several end-products for increased valorisation)
• Separation of heavy metal rich fractions from biomass 
• Communicate with stakeholders along the entire cultivation seaweed value chain and stay updated on national/international regulations (monitoring, restoration)
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in marine biology, biochemistry or biotechnology for ecological or biochemical studies of marine micro- and/or macroalgae. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• You must have hands on experience with methods for in in situ and laboratory methods/observations to measure phytoplankton/macroalgal biomass and health status with focus on one/several topics related to biodiversity, biochemical composition, primary production and function)
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works
• Excellent written and oral English skills
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• A MSc with experience from cross disciplinary work using enabling technology for marine ecology
• Experience in algal systematics, pigment and sugar chemistry, statistics methods, user/making codes in R or Python
• Experience using of underwater mobile platforms (e.g. pilot experience using Remotely Operated Vehicles) is beneficial
• Experience with seaweed hatcheries and cultivation
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian equivalent level A2Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are/have: 

• Hands on and highly motivated to use your PhD project as a contribution for a better marine nature management locally and internationally (core of Remedies project)
• Demonstrated teamwork skills with ability to work closely as part of collegial teams, and to contribute to a good and inclusive working environment
• Excellent communication skills
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• Exciting and challenging tasks in a strong international academic environment
• Opportunity to join the NTNU Observation Pyramid team that includes several departments and faculties, working locally, nationally and internationally
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

Candidates will be evaluated based on documented qualifications. We encourage qualified candidates to apply regardless of their gender identity, ability status, or cultural, ethnic, or religious background. We especially encourage upcoming early career academics and candidates from underrepresented groups to apply. To develop an inclusive and vibrant departmental culture, the Department of Biology maintains a standing committee focused on diversity, equality, and inclusivity.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Biology within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

Aachman, Professor in biopolymer interaction at IBT finn.l.aachmann@ntnu.no. jobs.occupation: Hardware Reliability Manager
jobs.description:
Nofence is a Norwegian scale-up that has built the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock. As we aim to revolutionize livestock management, we need top-notch competence in our Engineering team, and we are now looking for an Hardware Reliability Manager for our Hardware Reliability Team.

Hardware Reliability Team
Our Hardware Reliability Team works with quality at both ends of our product life cycle. First: Validation of new livestock product designs, and second: monitoring and identifying failures on products in the field. These tasks are split into two disciplines: validation and failure analysis. As Hardware Reliability Manager, you will lead both of these teams. You will have a holistic view of the real-life conditions of our products, and ensure that these conditions are replicated in the lab. What can not be replicated in the lab has to be validated in the field on test farms around the globe. You will also monitor product performance, coordinate field investigations, and recommend mitigations of quality issues together with other stakeholders.

Your main responsibilities will be:
• 
Shape the overall validation and quality strategy to match business goals and risk tolerance.

• 
Lead the Hardware Reliability Team across new and existing products - setting priorities, allocating resources across projects, clearing roadblocks, and keeping the team on track.

• 
Deliver clear, structured reporting on test progress, pass/fail metrics, and overall quality status.

• 
Own end-to-end mechanical, electronics, and embedded validation plans from early product development through mass production and failure analysis.

• 
Serve as a service point for internal stakeholders on validation and product quality.

• 
Plan, conduct, and execute field testing under real-world operating conditions to validate product performance and catch issue trends early.

• 
Monitor collar performance in the field after we release the product.

• 
Coordinate validation activities delivered to the engineering and manufacturing teams.

We are looking for someone who has:
• 
Bachelor or Master degree in engineering or another relevant degree

• 
Experience with leading engineering activities within hardware and software

• 
Experience with leading cross-functional teams at a technical level

• 
Excellent analytical skills

• 
Proven project management skills

• 
Knowledge of international testing standards

We are looking for someone who is:
• 
Motivated by working in an autonomous cross-functional team.

• 
Thrives in a fast-paced development environment and can rapidly assess and prioritize critical issues.

• 
Structured with the ability to bridge the gap between engineers and internal and external stakeholders.

• 
Willing and able to travel across the Nordic region and internationally to meet with end-users and colleagues.

• 
Comfortable working in an English-speaking environment.

About Nofence
Managing livestock has always been a challenge. Humanity has tried everything from herding with dogs to walling the animals in with barbed wire, electric, and wooden fences, but these are costly and time-consuming solutions and often in conflict with the local wildlife. It has also left vast areas of potential pasture overgrown and underutilized.

Until now.

Enter virtual fences. What started as a small group of farmers and engineers with a big idea has become Nofence – the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellows in Educational Measurement
jobs.description:
Job description
Applications are invited for 1-2 full time positions for three- to four-years as Postdoctoral Fellows at the Centre for Research on Equality in Education (CREATE), Faculty of Educational Sciences, University of Oslo, Norway. The positions have a double affiliation with the Centre for Educational Measurement (CEMO).

CREATE is an interdisciplinary Centre of Excellence funded by the Research Council of Norway with the objective to generate novel knowledge about how to reduce inequalities in education. The interdisciplinary center integrates researchers with substantive expertise from education, psychology, sociology, economics, and genetics, and methodological expertise from educational measurement, psychometrics, econometrics, statistics, and biostatistics. The Postdoctoral Fellowships are affiliated with CREATE’s research strand 3 «Addressing key methodological challenges».  

CEMO provides a stimulating research environment by bringing internationally renowned substantive and methodological experts together. Research at CEMO combines basic research and applications of advanced measurement techniques to solve core educational problems. CEMO also contributes to the development of measurement competence through teaching and outreach.
More about the positions
The positions are tied to strand 3 of CREATE, which aims to develop novel methods and statistical software that are tailor-made to the research questions and data of CREATE. 

The successful candidate will conduct advanced methodological and psychometric research. Potential research areas include (a) instructional sensitivity and opportunity to learn in international large-scale assessments in education, (b) estimation and inference methods for weighted generalized structural equation models with mixed continuous and discrete data in longitudinal settings, and (c) advancing research synthesis and meta-analytic methods, for instance, to investigate digital inequalities in education using international large-scale assessment data.

The appointments are full-time positions and made for a period of three years, 10% of which is devoted to required duties, usually in the form of teaching activities. If there is a good match between the candidate’s competence and the teaching needs at CEMO, the positions may be extended to four years, 25% of which is devoted to required duties, usually in the form of teaching activities and supervision. For these positions, the teaching activities will be part of CEMO’s master’s programme in Assessment, Measurement and Evaluation.

The main purpose of the fellowship is to build a research profile and competence that qualifies the postdoctoral fellow to apply for a position as associate professor within their disciplines. The position may also provide other competence with relevance for the postdoctoral fellow's further career.

If the Postdoctoral Fellow does not already have educational qualifications that meet the requirements for an associate professor position, UiO shall facilitate the acquisition of such competence during the employment period.

A career plan shall be developed for the Postdoctoral Fellow, specifying the competencies the Postdoctoral Fellow should acquire. UiO is responsible for following up on the career plan and ensuring that the Postdoctoral Fellow has access to career guidance throughout the postdoctoral term.
Qualification requirements
• Applicants must hold a degree equivalent to a Norwegian doctoral degree in one of the social and behavioral sciences, statistics, or computer science applying and/or developing advanced quantitative methods. The doctoral dissertation must have been submitted for evaluation by the application deadline. Appointment is dependent on the public defense of the doctoral thesis being approved
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English 
• Demonstrated fit to one of the three research areas (a) to (c) listed above
• Proficiency in programming and data analysis in the statistical software environment R, Python, or other relevant programming languages, as evidenced in relevant courses or publication(s)
Applicants will be evaluated as a function of the fit between their qualifications and the research area they apply for. The following qualifications will count in the assessment of the applicants:

• For research area (a), prior experience with IRT/mixed-effects logistic regression and international large-scale assessments in education
• For research area (b), prior experience with latent variable models and Monte Carlo simulation studies
• For research area (c), prior experience with meta-analysis/research synthesis and international large-scale assessment dataPersonal skills
• Creativity and ability to work independently 
• Self-motivated, eager to learn and ready to tackle and deal with challenges
• Able to collaborate with others 
Personal suitability and motivation for the position will be emphasized.
We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. 

We hope you will apply for the position with us.
We offer
• Salary NOK 595 000 - 670 000 per annum depending on qualifications in position as Postdoctoral Research Fellow (position code 1352). From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund
• A professionally stimulating work environment
• An interdisciplinary and international work environment, recognized as a Centre of Excellence
• Attractive welfare benefits 
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemesHow to apply
The application must include:

• Cover letter (maximum two pages), including a statement of motivation and your fit with one of the research areas (a) to (c) listed above 
• CV (summarizing education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative experience and other qualifying activity)
• Copy of PhD Diploma or documentation of thesis submission. Applicants who have not yet defended their PhD dissertation need to include an advisor's letter confirming specific expectations about when the degree will be received
• Copy of the PhD thesis 
• Copies of educational certificates (academic transcripts only)
• A complete list of publications
• List of reference persons: 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number)
The application with attachments must be delivered in our electronic recruiting system Jobbnorge. Foreign applicants are advised to attach an explanation of their University's grading system. Please note that all documents should be in English (or a Scandinavian language).

Incomplete applications will not be assessed. 

In assessing the applicants, special emphasis will be placed on the documented, academic qualifications, as well as the candidates motivation and personal suitability. Interviews with the best qualified candidates will be arranged.

It is expected that the successful candidate will be able to complete the project in the course of the period of employment.
Formal regulations
Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian) and the guidelines and regulations for appointments to Postdoctoral Fellowships at the University of Oslo.

No one can be appointed for more than one Postdoctoral Fellow period at the University of Oslo.

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.

The University of Oslo has an agreement for all employees, aiming to secure rights to research results etc.

Drivers license and ability to travel abroad.

Managing livestock has always been a challenge. jobs.occupation: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Six Robotics
At Six Robotics, we build intelligent software that gives Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) the ability to collaborate, adapt on the fly, and execute missions that were previously impossible.

From our base in Oslo, our team of 90+ engineers, researchers, and defence specialists develops our autonomy and swarm platform, used by both government and industry. Working closely with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI) and end users, we move quickly from ideas to field deployment, solving problems where software meets the real world.

The challenges we work on don’t come with existing playbooks. They demand deep technical thinking, close collaboration across disciplines, and the ability to learn quickly as both the technology and the company evolve.

At Six Robotics, every person executes with precision, adapts to changing conditions, and strengthens the team. If you’re excited about building systems that matter and growing alongside talented people that push boundaries every day, you’ll find no better place to deliver real-world impact.

About The Role
At Six Robotics, our product department is built around a clear flow: needs emerge from our customers, are shaped into product features, and are then translated into engineering-ready functionality. As we scale, we are strengthening our Product Team to own this flow end-to-end. This role will build and own the bridge between these domains, ensuring that what we ship is not driven by ad-hoc requests, but by validated needs from the field, strong technical context, and disciplined product decisions.

As a Product Manager at Six Robotics, you will turn complex project needs, field feedback, and long-term strategy into a coherent, executable product direction. This is a hands-on, operational product role at the center of engineering, projects, and real-world UAV operations.

You will help define where our software product, Valkyrie, is going. Defining what gets built, and why, without abstracting away the reality and context the engineering teams need to succeed and understand.

This role is critical in bringing stability, clarity, and long-term focus to how Valkyrie evolves, while still adapting to real-world demands from customers, field operations, and live deployments.

You will work closely with the other Product Managers and report to the Chief of Product, bringing clarity to our Engineering Team Leads, release and project management, acting as the bridge that ensures we build the right capabilities, at the right time, for the right reasons.

What You Will Do
• 
Translate project and customer requirements into actionable product features: prioritize, scope, and refine features so engineering can execute with clarity and confidence.

• 
Shape the product roadmap alongside the Head of Product: contribute to the vision, break it down into a detailed plan, and ensure it drives meaningful, deliverable work.

• 
Bring clarity to engineering to ensure we build the right features: minimize product debt, reduce ad-hoc feature work, and safeguard long-term product quality.

• 
Own operational product execution: track progress, manage priorities, and follow up on releases to keep product development structured and predictable.

• 
Maintain product clarity and coherence: oversee trade-offs, dependencies, and release content to ensure each feature delivers real value internally before reaching engineering.

• 
Validate and refine assumptions in the field: work and test the features with our field teams, to understand real-world performance and feed insights back into product decisions.

What we are looking for
We are looking for someone with exceptional structure and decision-making skills. We believe this person can confidently say no when needed, set direction, and still listen deeply to both the team and the customer. You thrive in ambiguity, bringing discipline and method where things feel uncertain, and you take ownership not just of your own work, but across teams and interfaces. You are comfortable challenging customers constructively, asking why they want something, and translating that into what is actually feasible and valuable for engineering to build. At the same time, you are hands-on, willing to dive into the details when necessary, without ever losing sight of priorities or long-term outcomes.

We believe the right candidate brings
• 
Proven experience working on the development of mission-critical software products, with clear ownership from idea to delivery.

• 
Strong understanding of the full product lifecycle - from requirements and specification to delivery, validation, and iteration.

• 
Strong background in building software products, with the ability to collaborate with engineers while keeping problems concrete and solvable.

• 
Experience in structuring and governing product flow - balancing prioritization, planning, dependencies, and release coordination.

• 
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex customer needs into clear engineering context, without losing the bigger picture.

• 
A competitive drive and delivery mindset. You care about outcomes, not just process.

• 
Fluency in English (Norwegian not required).

Nice-to-haves:

• 
Experience with UAVs, autonomy systems, robotics, or defence-related technology.

• 
Exposure to hardware-software integrated products or field-deployed systems.

Why you should join
• 
Build at the edge of what’s possible: You’ll work on problems the industry hasn’t solved yet, alongside people who are pushing the boundaries of autonomy, AI, and robotics.

• 
Grow as fast as the company: We believe that chance favours those in motion. The role you’re hired into is just the starting point. As Six Robotics evolves, so will your scope, your responsibilities, and your opportunities.

• 
Work with exceptional people: Surround yourself with people who raise your own standards. You’ll join a team of ambitious engineers and operators who care deeply about the quality of their work. Expectations are high, but so is the willingness to help each other improve.

• 
Ship work that matters. The things you build don't stay in a demo environment. They get deployed, tested, and used where reliability and performance genuinely matter.

• 
Supported by great benefits. Alongside meaningful work, we offer competitive compensation, equity potential, strong pension and insurance plans, gadget budgets, modern equipment, panoramic offices, and the flexibility you need to do your best work.

Our Recruitment Process
We want hiring to be transparent and respectful of your time. We aim to move with momentum while making thoughtful hiring decisions - because every new team member matters.

Our process typically includes:

• 
Initial phone screening (30 min): A conversation about your background, motivation, and the role.

• 
First interview (45 min): Meet the hiring team, learn more about Six Robotics, and discuss your experience.

• 
Second interview (60–90 min): A technical discussion/Case interview, typically including a take-home assignment with a case presentation.

• 
Final interview (45 min): Meet members of our leadership team to align expectations and answer any remaining questions.

Reference checks are conducted before an offer is finalized. We review applications continuously, so don't leave us hanging. Send us your application today!

Our Commitment to Inclusion
At Six Robotics, we are committed to creating a workplace built on respect, integrity, and collaboration. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we believe that diversity within our team strengthens both our work and our culture. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply and help us build technology that makes a real impact.

Security Clearance Requirement
All employees at Six Robotics must be eligible for security clearance. Some roles might require a high level of clearance, depending on the nature of the work. If you are hired, we’ll guide you through any required authorization or clearance process as part of your onboarding. Previous authorization or clearance is not required, but all candidates must be eligible to obtain the necessary approvals if required for their role.
